transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I am here because my family and my friends made me come, all because I refuse to just sit down and shut up about it. They keep waving these bank papers in my face, pointing at the lines and telling me that the papers prove nothing was taken from me. But anybody can fake a piece of paper, you know? For over a year now, way over a year, I have known exactly what they are doing. They are hiding my money. It is my money, and they took it, and now they are using all this stuff to cover it up. 

They think I do not notice, but I see them using these random bills that suddenly cost way more than they should, and suddenly everybody is talking about fundraisers and donating to this and that, and making all these big trip plans. Trip plans! Where do they get the money for trips, huh? It is all a big cover-up to hide my cash. They are just moving it around so I cannot find it. So yeah, I keep confronting them. I have to. I follow them into the kitchen, I call them on the phone, I will not let them rest because I have to keep confronting them until they finally break down and tell the truth about where my money went.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Voices? Like in my head or something? No, no, I do not have anything like that going on. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it is better than fine, I hear everything. Sometimes I think I hear too much, you know, just regular noises like the fridge humming all night or the neighbors dog barking two whole streets over. But no, no voices that are not really there. I know some people get that, like they hear someone talking when nobody is even in the room, but that has never ever happened to me. Not even once. I mean, I hear people mumbling a lot, people do not speak up like they used to, they just mutter under their breath and you have to ask them to repeat themselves three times just to get a straight answer out of them. But that is just them being quiet and sneaky, not me hearing things that do not exist. I only hear what is actually spoken out loud by real people. So if anyone tried to tell you I was hearing voices, they are just making that up, because my ears work just perfectly and I only hear real things.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energized, needed much less sleep than usual, and felt like your thoughts were racing?

Energized? Like, bouncing off the walls? No, not really. I mean, I don't get a lot of sleep, but that's because I can't afford to sleep, you know? If I close my eyes for too long, who knows what they're doing with my money? I have to stay up and check the accounts, and I have to listen at the door to see if they're whispering about the trips they're planning with my cash. So, yeah, I'm awake a lot, but I'm tired. I'm so exhausted all the time. It's not like I have this magical energy where I just want to clean the whole house or run a marathon. It's just... I'm awake because I have to be. 

And racing thoughts? I don't know what you mean by racing. My thoughts are focused. Very, very focused. I'm just trying to figure out the puzzle, you know? Connecting the dots. Like, why did my sister suddenly buy a new car? Where did she get the down payment? I'm thinking about that, and I'm thinking about the bank statements, and I'm thinking about how they always change the subject when I ask about the inheritance. So, my mind is busy, sure. It's always busy because there's so much to keep track of, so many lies to untangle. But it's not racing like it's out of control. It's just doing its job, trying to protect what's mine. I don't have time for my mind to go off on weird tangents. I have to stay sharp. If I don't stay sharp, they win. So no, no weird energy bursts or anything like that. Just me, trying to stay awake so they don't rob me blind while I'm snoring.
Apart from feeling exhausted and stressed about this situation, have you been experiencing a persistent low or depressed mood, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Depressed? Like, sad and crying all the time? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm angry. I am so, so angry and frustrated, but I'm not sitting around crying into my pillow, if that's what you mean. I don't have time to be depressed. How could I even sit around feeling sorry for myself when there is this massive conspiracy happening right under my nose? 

As for losing interest in things... well, I guess I don't really do the things I used to do, but it's not because I lost interest. It's because I literally do not have the time. I used to like doing puzzles, you know, the big thousand-piece ones? I'd sit at the kitchen table for hours. And I used to like watching those home improvement shows, seeing how they fix up houses. But I haven't done a puzzle or turned on the TV for anything other than the news in... well, in over a year. Ever since I figured out what they were doing with my money. 

But it's not like I don't *want* to do those things. I just can't. If I sit down to do a puzzle, that's an hour I'm not checking the bank statements. That's an hour I'm not cross-referencing my sister's grocery receipts to see if she's using my cash to buy expensive steaks. Do you know how much a good steak costs these days? A lot. And she's eating them twice a week! Where does that money come from? Exactly. So, no, I'm not depressed and I haven't lost interest. I've just had to reprioritize. My whole life right now has to be about getting to the bottom of this. I have to be vigilant. If I let my guard down to go watch a TV show or put together a picture of a kitten in a basket, they win. And I am absolutely not going to let them win. So, no, I'm not depressed. I'm just busy. Very, very busy trying to get my money back.
Have you been diagnosed with any physical illnesses or neurological conditions?

Physical illnesses? Like... like my body being sick? Or my brain having some kind of disease? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, my body is perfectly healthy. Well, as healthy as it can be when you're under this much stress, right? I mean, I get headaches sometimes, but who wouldn't get headaches when they're staring at numbers and receipts for fourteen hours a day? It's just eye strain, really. And maybe some tension in my neck, right here at the base of my skull, because I'm always hunched over the desk trying to make sure the math adds up. But no doctor has ever told me I have a disease or a condition or anything. 

I haven't even been to a regular doctor in... gosh, it has to be three years now. Because, honestly, what are they going to do? They take your blood pressure, they tell you to eat more vegetables, and then they charge you a fortune. And I can't be throwing money away on copays when my own family is siphoning off my savings. Every dollar counts right now. Plus, you never know who they're talking to. What if my sister called the clinic? What if she told them to put something in my chart to make me look crazy, just so she could get power of attorney? You hear about that happening all the time. People just getting locked up because a relative wants their estate. So I stay away from doctors. Well, except for you, obviously, because they made me come here. 

But no, my brain is fine. My nerves are fine. No neurological whatever-you-called-it. My hands don't shake, I don't have seizures, I don't faint. I am completely physically capable. In fact, I have to be in top physical shape just to keep up with all the investigating I'm doing. If I was sick, I'd have to stay in bed, and if I stayed in bed, they would clean out my accounts in a week. So I make sure I take my vitamins, I drink a lot of water, and I stay healthy. Because if my body gives out, they get away with it. And I am not giving them that satisfaction. So no, no physical illnesses at all. I am perfectly fine in that department.
Have you ever felt like other people can read your mind or hear your thoughts out loud?

Read my mind? Like... like they have some kind of superpower or something? No, no, that's just silly. I mean, if my sister could read my mind, she would have known I moved the lockbox key from under the bathroom sink to the inside of the flour jar in the kitchen, right? But she didn't know. I know she didn't because I put a little piece of tape on the flour jar lid, and it hasn't been broken. So no, nobody is hearing my thoughts out loud. That's just movie stuff. 

My thoughts are locked up tight right here in my own head. They don't need to read my mind anyway, because they're always snooping the old-fashioned way. Like, just last Tuesday, I saw the mail had been tampered with. The flap on the envelope from the bank was all wrinkled—you know how it gets when someone steams it open and tries to glue it back down? They think I'm stupid. I mean, I know I didn't finish high school, but I'm not an idiot. I know how glue works. I know what a steamed envelope looks like. 

So they don't need to hear my thoughts out loud when they can just steal my mail or listen at my bedroom door. I catch them doing that, you know. I'll be sitting on my bed, adding up the numbers in my notebook, and I'll see the shadow of feet under the door crack. They're just standing there in the hallway, holding their breath, trying to hear if I'm on the phone with the police or a lawyer or something. That's why I started playing the radio real low, just on a static station, to muffle the sound of my calculator clicking. You have to think ahead of them. 

But my actual thoughts? Inside my brain? No, nobody can hear those. If they could hear what I was thinking, they'd be terrified, because they would know exactly how close I am to proving the whole thing. They'd know I have the grocery receipts. They'd know I'm onto the fact that she's hiding the cash in something else. But no, they can't read my mind. I don't have any weird magic stuff going on. It's just a regular brain, working overtime to stop a bunch of thieves from taking every last dime I have.
